overview: 361 Degrees International Limited, founded in 2003 and listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2009, is a vertically integrated PRC sportswear company that designs, develops, manufactures and distributes footwear, apparel and accessories under the 361º brand, with a dedicated 361º Kids children's sportswear line and a small stake in the Finnish outdoor brand ONEWAY. The company positions itself as a 'professional, youthful, and internationalised' mass-market sports brand focused on running and basketball, sold through a nationwide distributor network, a growing direct e-commerce channel, and an expanding international footprint across the Americas, Europe and Belt-and-Road markets. It is one of the second tier of major Chinese domestic sportswear groups behind ANTA Sports and Li Ning, running roughly level with or slightly ahead of Xtep on profitability.

business_model.summary: 361º earns revenue from wholesale/distributor sales of branded footwear and apparel to a nationwide network of exclusive regional distributors and authorised retailers (order-driven via quarterly trade fairs held ~6 months ahead of delivery), supplemented by a fast-growing direct e-commerce business and a children's sportswear sub-brand (361º Kids) that is run as a largely separate business unit. Production is a hybrid of in-house manufacturing (~35.6% of footwear, ~18.5% of apparel at two self-owned Fujian facilities) and OEM outsourcing, giving flexibility while protecting proprietary technology on flagship products.

channel_mix.name: E-commerce
channel_mix.trend: growing (+25.9% YoY FY2025; overseas cross-border e-commerce +140% YoY H1 2026)

channel_mix.name: Offline distributor/retail network
channel_mix.trend: stable, channel mix shifting to malls/Super Premium Stores

business_model.customer_type: B2B wholesale to exclusive regional distributors and authorised retailers in China, plus direct-to-consumer via owned e-commerce storefronts and a small but growing network of overseas offline points-of-sale (1,253 as of FY2025)
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly PRC domestic (Chinese mainland core brand: 5,394 stores, ~76% in third-tier-or-lower cities); international expansion still small in revenue terms but growing fast (overseas retail sales +80% YoY in H1 2026) across the Americas, Europe, Southeast Asia and Belt-and-Road markets

competitive_position.market_position: Fourth-largest of the major domestic Chinese sportswear groups by revenue, well behind ANTA (~RMB87bn FY2025 revenue scale) and Li Ning, but delivering the fastest profit growth among the big four in H1 2026 and now generating higher net profit than Xtep (RMB926m vs RMB818m in H1 2026) despite lower revenue. Domestic brands (ANTA, Li Ning, Xtep, 361º) have collectively grown China sportswear market share from under 30% (2015) to roughly 50% (2025) at the expense of Nike and Adidas.

moat_factors.description: Long-running Asian Games/Asian Winter Games partnerships (5th consecutive Games, first brand to sponsor both Asian Games and Asian Winter Games), global ambassadors (Nikola Jokić, Aaron Gordon, Spencer Dinwiddie), and a dense marathon/grassroots sponsorship calendar build mass-market recognition, though brand strength trails ANTA and Li Ning
'Quality-for-money' professional product strategy targets price-sensitive lower-tier city consumers (76% of mainland stores in tier-3-or-below cities), a demographic less contested by premium players

1,101 patents, in-house production of technically complex footwear (CQT carbon-critical midsole technology, proprietary cushioning platforms) alongside OEM outsourcing provides some cost and IP control; recent acquisition of OEM plant/machinery and patents (late 2025) deepens this
Exclusive regional distributorship system with annual renewals creates some channel stickiness, though the company depends heavily on third parties it does not control directly
Dedicated children's sportswear sub-brand with first-mover positioning, benefiting from pro-natalist policy and youth sports participation tailwinds

weaknesses: Materially smaller scale than ANTA and Li Ning, limiting marketing/R&D budgets and bargaining power with suppliers and landlords
Heavy reliance on third-party distributors and authorised retailers over whom the Group has limited direct operating control
Brand skews toward lower-tier cities and value segment, which carries lower pricing power and margin ceiling versus premium domestic or international brands
International business still nascent in absolute revenue terms despite high growth rates
Kids apparel category revenue declined in FY2025 (-7.5%), showing uneven execution within the kids segment

growth_drivers: E-commerce and new instant-retail integrations (Meituan Flash Buy/Group Buy, Taobao Flash Sale, JD Instant Delivery) expanding digital reach and driving ecommerce to ~29.5% of FY2025 revenue
361º Super Premium Store rollout (127 stores at FY2025-end, 188 by H1 2026) as a higher-productivity retail format, including first overseas Super Premium Store in Cambodia

International expansion: overseas retail sales +80% YoY and cross-border e-commerce +140% YoY in H1 2026, funded in part by the May 2026 HK$610m placement/subscription (80% earmarked for overseas expansion)
361º Kids segment benefiting from pro-natalist policy support, expanded school sports investment, and extension of target age range to 16
Global sports-event sponsorship cycle (2026 Winter Olympics Milano-Cortina, FIFA World Cup, Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya, World Aquatics 2026-2029 partnership) raising international brand visibility
New category expansion into tennis, badminton, pickleball, cycling, women's fitness/yoga, and outdoor (ONEWAY outdoor brand) to diversify beyond running/basketball
Supportive PRC government policy agenda for the sports industry (targeting sports industry value >RMB7 trillion by 2030) and consumption-boosting initiatives
Deepening vertical integration via acquisition of OEM plant, machinery and patents (late 2025) to raise in-house production ratio and control costs

business.description: Reliance on exclusive third-party distributors and authorised retailers without direct operational control; non-compliance with brand/pricing/store-image standards could damage the brand
Products are discretionary; company explicitly flagged dampened consumer sentiment from US-China trade tensions during FY2025
ANTA and Li Ning have far larger scale and marketing budgets; Xtep and smaller players also compete for the same value-oriented consumer
FY2025 Kids Apparel revenue declined 7.5% YoY even as Kids Footwear grew strongly, indicating some execution unevenness

financial.description: Inventory turnover days rose from 87 (2021) to 117 (FY2025) and working capital turnover days rose from 114 to 192 over the same period, a trend worth monitoring even though it partially reversed in H1 2026

May 2026 top-up placement/subscription raised ~HK$610m but increased share count and a related party (chairman's family trust vehicle) was the vendor/subscriber, raising minor related-party/governance optics
Revenue and earnings are RMB-denominated while dividends are declared and likely received by many investors in HKD, introducing FX translation risk to shareholder returns

regulatory.risk: PRC consumption and retail policy shifts
regulatory.description: Business benefits from current supportive sports-industry policy; a reversal or weaker implementation of stimulus could remove a tailwind
US-China trade tensions and evolving tariff policy affect both consumer sentiment in China and the cost/competitiveness of the Group's growing overseas export and retail operations

macro.description: Revenue growth is tied to Chinese retail sales and consumer confidence, particularly in lower-tier cities where the core brand is concentrated
Management explicitly cited 'heightened geopolitical tensions' and global economic fragmentation as a 2026 risk factor affecting both domestic and international operations
Footwear/apparel input costs (rubber, synthetic materials, labour) and OEM capacity constraints can pressure gross margin, partially mitigated by in-house production and supplier relationships

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese sportswear retail sales showed a modest beat-expectations recovery in early 2026 (Jefferies forecast >5% YoY growth for Jan-Feb 2026) after a soft, warm-winter-affected Q4 2025; full-year 2025 China clothing/footwear/textile retail sales rose 3.2% to RMB1.52 trillion. Domestic brands (ANTA, Li Ning, Xtep, 361º) have structurally gained share from Nike/Adidas since the 2021 Xinjiang cotton episode, lifting combined domestic brand share to roughly 50% of the China sportswear market by 2025.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - sportswear is consumer discretionary and sensitive to Chinese retail/consumer confidence cycles, but benefits from secular health-and-wellness and youth-sports participation tailwinds that partially offset cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (very low gearing ratio of ~2-3% of total assets); indirect sensitivity through Chinese consumer credit conditions and property-market wealth effects on discretionary spending
key_input_costs: OEM manufacturing capacity and labour costs

recent_developments.event: Analyst coverage (Crosby/Emperor Capital) maintains Buy rating with price targets in the HK$7.30-7.80 range through March 2026, though share price volatility (reported -15.8%/-13.9% over six months in a May 2026 note) suggests the stock has pulled back from earlier 2026 highs

H1 2026 interim results: revenue +8.0% YoY to RMB6.16bn, profit attributable to equity holders +8.0% YoY to RMB925.9m, interim dividend of HK22.2 cents (45% payout ratio); overseas retail sales +80% YoY and cross-border e-commerce +140% YoY
Voluntary Q2 2026 trading update reported mid-to-high single-digit retail sales growth for the core brand, continued growth in Kids and e-commerce outperforming offline channels

Completed a HK$610-611 million top-up share placement and subscription (UBS as sole placing agent; vendor/subscriber tied to Chairman Ding Huihuang's family trust), with ~80% of proceeds earmarked for overseas market expansion and the remainder for working capital
Entered partnership with JD Instant Delivery, completing a '1+6' omnichannel instant-retail model across six online platforms integrated with offline stores
New phase of strategic cooperation agreement signed with the Olympic Council of Asia; global launch of Nikola Jokić's 'JOKER2' and Aaron Gordon's 'AG6' signature basketball shoes in the US
Charitable donations (RMB15m) following the Tai Po, Hong Kong fire disaster and earlier RMB8m following the Tibet earthquake (Jan 2025), reflecting active CSR/ESG engagement
Global partnership agreement signed with World Aquatics covering 2026-2029

Full-year results: revenue +10.6% YoY to RMB11.1bn, profit attributable to equity holders +14.0% YoY to RMB1,308.9m, ROE improved to 13.5%, full-year dividend payout ratio maintained at 45% (HK31.7 cents/share); acquisition of OEM plant, machinery and patents from two independent third parties to deepen vertical integration

items.notes: Expected to rise toward the upper end of the historical 2.9%-3.4% range due to scheduled increase in R&D activity in H2 2026

items.period: FY2026 (implied, consistent with FY2024/FY2025/H1 2026 track record)
items.notes: Company has held a stable 45% payout ratio for at least the last three reporting periods (FY2024, FY2025, H1 2026)

items.target: Continued acceleration of overseas offline network and cross-border e-commerce
items.notes: ~80% (~HK$488m) of May 2026 placement proceeds earmarked specifically for overseas market expansion, signalling a step-up in international investment intensity

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Ding Huihuang's H1 2026 statement describes a 'fragmented' global economy with heightened geopolitical tension but stresses that China's domestic sports consumption continues to be 'unleashed,' with event economy and outdoor sports as core growth drivers; management highlights omnichannel upgrading, deeper global expansion (overseas retail sales +80% YoY), and continued event-sponsorship investment (2026 Winter Olympics, FIFA World Cup, Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya) as the core 2026 strategic priorities, alongside ongoing technology-driven product development across running, basketball, women's sports and kids categories.

bull_case: Fastest profit growth among the 'big four' domestic Chinese sportswear brands in H1 2026, now surpassing Xtep in absolute net profit despite lower revenue, while trading at a smaller scale/valuation than ANTA or Li Ning

Rapidly growing e-commerce (+25.9% FY2025) and international business (+80% overseas retail, +140% cross-border e-commerce in H1 2026) provide diversification away from the mature mainland offline channel
Low gearing (~2-3%) and a consistent 45% dividend payout ratio offer a shareholder-friendly, conservatively financed balance sheet with room for continued capital return

Secular tailwinds from PRC health/wellness policy, pro-natalist/youth-sports initiatives benefiting 361º Kids, and a packed global sports-events calendar (2026 Winter Olympics, FIFA World Cup, Asian Games) support multi-year brand visibility and demand
361º Kids and value-oriented core brand are well positioned in lower-tier Chinese cities, a demographic less contested by premium domestic and international rivals
bear_case: Materially smaller scale than ANTA Sports and Li Ning limits marketing, R&D, and negotiating leverage, making long-term share gains against the top two more difficult
Heavy dependence on third-party distributors/retailers that the Group cannot directly control creates execution and brand-consistency risk
Products remain discretionary and sentiment-sensitive; management itself flagged US-China trade tensions dampening consumer sentiment toward non-essential goods in FY2025
Rising inventory and working-capital turnover days over FY2021-FY2025 (before a partial H1 2026 improvement) could signal softening sell-through or channel inventory buildup if the trend resumes

Recent related-party-linked share placement (chairman's family trust as vendor/subscriber) and resulting dilution, combined with reported share price weakness in mid-2026 despite strong fundamentals, warrant governance and sentiment monitoring
